brief.headline: Push for a 3–4% price reduction: they run an 8.5% net margin — 77% above the 4.8% peer median — leaving clear room to share the margin upside with us.

priceAsk.summary: Request a 3–4% reduction on rigid plastic packaging rates
priceAsk.target: Aim to close the gap toward the peer median margin of 4.8%, capturing part of their 8.5% net margin premium
priceAsk.basis: Triveni's 8.5% net margin is 77% higher than the 4.8% peer median for Pharma Packaging, and their 14.5% EBITDA margin confirms operational cushion. HDPE resin import unit value stands at 87.61 ₹/kg per UN Comtrade, giving us a raw-material benchmark to anchor cost discussions.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Tighten terms from 45 Days After Receipt to 30 days, with a stretch goal of 15 additional days (net 15)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 30 days releases ₹2.15 L in working capital; a further 15-day acceleration frees an additional ₹1.08 L.

brief.financialLeverage: Triveni is financially strong — 0.00x debt-to-equity, 75.84x interest coverage, and a 4/10 Probe42 score (B health rating, 70/100). Their 8.5% net margin is 77% above the 4.8% peer median, and their 14.5% EBITDA margin gives ample pricing headroom. However, our ₹26.17 L spend is only 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue, so we have limited standalone leverage. They also carry EPF payment delays as a risk flag. We can push hard on price and terms because their margins and balance sheet are robust, but we must credibly threaten volume consolidation or competition from alternates (Mold-Tek, Manjushree) to overcome our small-customer disadvantage.

evidence.point: Triveni earns an 8.5% net margin, 77% higher than the 4.8% peer median
Their EBITDA margin of 14.5% confirms strong operational profitability
Zero debt gives them a 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio and 75.84x interest coverage
We represent only 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue at ₹26.17 L annual spend
HDPE resin import unit value benchmark is 87.61 ₹/kg
Shortening payment terms to 30 days frees ₹2.15 L; a further 15-day cut releases another ₹1.08 L

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader with pharma capability (pails, containers, bottles, closures); A-rated health — a robust, credible second source for our packaging.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter specializing in pharma bottles, caps, and preforms — the top second-source candidate to compete against Triveni.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) offering a direct fit for PET bottles, though D-rated health requires careful vetting.

risks: Our ₹26.17 L spend is only 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue — low standalone leverage means we must bundle volume, commit multi-year, or credibly compete them with Mold-Tek or Manjushree to gain traction.
They have EPF payment delays flagged as a risk — monitor compliance and delivery reliability closely, especially if we scale volume.

Their receivable days are 102d vs a 93d peer median, and cash conversion cycle is 124d vs 114d — they may resist shorter payment terms because their working capital is already stretched relative to peers.
Probe42 financial score of 4/10 and return on capital of 6.6% (vs 12.6% peer median) suggest weaker asset efficiency — confirm operational stability before committing larger volumes.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we've noticed your 8.5% net margin is well above the 4.8% industry median — let's talk about how we can share some of that upside through better pricing and tighter payment terms.
